conventions.convention: States are finite arrays over R or C, with order d≥2 and positive physical dimensions; the Frobenius pairing conjugates its first argument, and vectorization uses fixed lexicographic index order.

Open-boundary TT presentations have boundary bond sizes one. Periodic presentations use a trace with r_d=r_0 and are converted exactly to open-boundary form before applying canonical environment arguments.
The ground-vector rule projects standard basis vectors onto the lowest eigenspace in order, normalizes the first nonzero projection, and fixes its first nonzero coordinate to be positive real.

Mixed canonical gauge means left-isometric cores strictly left of the center and right-isometric cores strictly right of it; QR removes exactly dependent directions and preserves the represented tensor.

Sweeps use exact arithmetic, exact local ground solves and lossless two-site SVD splits. Optional rank-cap rounding occurs only after the complete forward/backward sweep; a candidate is accepted and normalized only if its recorded root-sum-square tail is less than one.

The stationarity conclusion assumes fixed bond dimensions and convergence at every update stage, in one consistent gauge, to a single normalized canonical core tuple; endpoint convergence alone is not the stated hypothesis.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite open-boundary TT in mixed gauge about a one-site or two-site center, the fixed-environment center embedding satisfies E*E=I. For Hermitian H, H_eff=E*HE is Hermitian and ⟨Ex,HEx⟩_F=x*H_eff x.

For A*=A over R or C and m≥1, its Rayleigh quotient has minimum equal to its least eigenvalue, with minimizers precisely the nonzero vectors in the lowest eigenspace; the stated projection and phase rule selects a deterministic unit minimizer.

A nonzero finite open-boundary TT admits an exact rank-revealing QR transformation about any selected one-site or two-site center window, preserving its array, making the exterior cores left- and right-isometric, and removing only exactly dependent directions.

Replacing a unit center vector in an isometric mixed-canonical embedding by the deterministic unit ground vector of E*HE preserves normalization and does not increase global Rayleigh energy, before any bond truncation.
For a finite self-adjoint H and unit finite tensor states ψ and φ, |⟨ψ,Hψ⟩_F−⟨φ,Hφ⟩_F|≤2||H||_op ||ψ−φ||_F.
A periodic MPS of order d≥2 with positive cyclic bond sizes has an exactly equal open-boundary TT presentation with internal bond sizes s_k=r_k r_0, using the specified carried pair indices.

After one exact unrounded forward/backward sweep, exact TT rounding with nonnegative integer rank caps and recorded total tail τ<1 has nonzero output; its normalized output φ satisfies E_H(φ)≤E_H(ψ_0)+4||H||_op τ and E_H(φ)−E_H(ψ_*)≤4||H||_op τ.

published_dependencies.used_for: Self-adjointness and the implication that self-adjoint endomorphisms are normal.
Identifying Hermitian matrices with self-adjoint endomorphisms in the standard orthonormal basis.
The real-field Rayleigh quotient convention in the ground-vector lemma.
Its decreasing-eigenvalue convention and k=m case give the real least-eigenvalue Rayleigh minimum.
A real orthonormal eigenbasis and the characterization of Rayleigh minimizers by their spectral coefficients.
A complex orthonormal eigenbasis; the owned proof separately establishes reality of Hermitian eigenvalues.
Constructing the unique orthogonal projection onto the lowest eigenspace.
Bounding ||Hv|| by ||H||_op ||v|| in the normalized-energy perturbation proof; the tensor domain is nonzero.
Bounding both terms in the expanded energy difference. The consumer explicitly accounts for the supplier's opposite inner-product argument convention.
Orthonormalizing the independent columns retained by the exact rank-revealing scan.
Exact compact SVDs for lossless two-site splitting and the external TT-rounding suppliers.
Proving rounded-output nonvanishing when τ<1 and bounding the distance after normalization.

concerns.concern: Verification step 1.1 says “Thus |00⟩ is the unique unit ground vector with energy −3”. The eigenspace is one-dimensional, but −|00⟩ is also a unit ground vector over R, and arbitrary unit phases are possible over C. The deterministic rule does select exactly |00⟩, so the computed sweep result is sound; the uniqueness wording needs an explicit phase qualification.

The Example says “The exact two-site solve returns the unique ground state ψ”. States were defined as normalized arrays, without identifying global phases, so uniqueness literally holds only up to phase. Verification step 2.1 correctly proves that the deterministic projection rule selects exactly the displayed ψ. Clarify that the ground eigenspace is one-dimensional or that uniqueness is up to phase.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page, finite-array and TT-core definitions, exact rounding procedure, and complete root-sum-square theorem proof against the consumer uses. Contraction order, conjugate-first pairing, gauge orientations, exact arithmetic and recorded tails agree. The supplier permits nonnegative rank caps; the algorithm uses positive caps, while the separate truncation theorem permits zero caps and requires τ<1 before normalization. The consumer uses the supplier's error bound without strengthening it and supplies its own normalization and energy estimates.
